summary: Build practical AI governance, risk, and responsible AI adoption skills with frameworks, controls, and workshop-based templates.
lede: AI governance training helps professionals responsible for AI use assess risks and establish oversight across the AI lifecycle. Learners practice classifying use cases, building risk registers, mapping policy controls, reviewing bias and fairness concerns, and setting monitoring and escalation workflows. It is suited to governance, compliance, model risk, audit, and risk professionals who need to document and report AI decisions.
audienceIntro: This course is designed for professionals who need to govern AI use, review risk, and support responsible adoption decisions across the AI lifecycle.
prerequisites: Recommended prerequisites for this intermediate course include working knowledge of AI or analytics projects, familiarity with basic risk management concepts, and experience reviewing policies, controls, or technology change requests. You do not need to code, but you should be comfortable reading governance documents, interpreting risk findings, and discussing digital workflow controls with technical teams. A laptop is required for workshop exercises using templates, review checklists, and governance artefacts.
